Return dominant water types

Source: R/calculations.R
dominant_water_types.Rd

Find the dominant waters type in a group of samples, but only if there are more than n samples with a valid water type. HCO3 and HCO3* types are treated as equivalent. Water types are considered dominant if they are in > p proportion of samples.

Usage

dominant_water_types(samples, n = 5, p = 0.75)

Arguments

samples

Data frame with at least a water_type column.

n

Numeric. Minimum number of samples needed to determine dominant water types.

p

Numeric. Proportion of samples with a given water type for it to be considered dominant.

Value

Character vector of dominant water types

Examples

wt <- data.frame(
  water_type = c(
    "Mg-Na-Ca-HCO3-SO4",
    "Mg-Na-Ca-HCO3-SO4",
    "Mg-Na-Ca",
    "Ca-Mg-HCO3-SO4",
    "Ca-Mg-HCO3-SO4",
    "Mg-Na",
    "Mg-Na",
    "Ca-Mg-Na")
  )
dominant_water_types(wt)
#> [1] "Mg-Na-Ca"          "Ca-Mg-HCO3-SO4"    "Mg-Na"            
#> [4] "Mg-Na-Ca-HCO3-SO4"
